$Comment: Dunewalker Ashkar, the Howling Sands quest giver, standing beside an Outlander hunter camp.
Where: the world named 'default', which is the persistent world players log into, never an
instance - a bare word under Match is an exact name. If your server's main world has another
name, change it here (or override this placement by id from your own pack).
Anchor.Structure attaches the placement to a worldgen spawn marker, so Ashkar lands at the first
camp the world generates and streams in rather than at fixed coordinates. MarkerIds is an exact,
case-insensitive allow-list; run /mmonpc structures in game to see the marker ids a world has
actually loaded before authoring one. The allow-list is FAIL-CLOSED, so a typo leaves Ashkar
absent rather than standing beside every marker in the world.
Limits: one per world, and every matching marker is used. Raise MaxPerWorld to stand one at
every matching camp instead.
Identity.Role names the NPC role this placement spawns. Ashkar's look and nameplate live in that
role file (Server/NPC/Roles/Passive/Guide_Sands.json), which this pack ships, so re-dress him
there rather than here. Point Role at a different role id to stand somebody else at the camps.
This placement authors no Identity.NpcId, so the character IS its role: the pack's quests
name Guide_Sands as their npcViewId, the dialogue below is automatically with him, and a talk
step credits against it. Author an NpcId to make this standing a character of its own that
nothing else answers to.
Press F opens Ashkar's own dialogue. The conversation is automatically WITH Ashkar: the header
name, @self, the talk credit and every quest-aware line in it all read this placement's own
identity, so nothing here restates his npc id. That same id is what the pack's quests bind as
their npcViewId, and what the campaign's earlier 'go and meet Ashkar' step reports back to.
Name: Guide_Sands
